script.title: The Rocket That Burns Thirteen Tonnes of Fuel Every Second
script.description: A comparison of the Saturn V and the Space Launch System reveals the immense power required for lunar exploration. These rockets generate millions of newtons of thrust to lift their massive fuel loads into orbit.
script.hook_card: The most powerful machines ever built.

shots.narration: The Saturn V rocket burned roughly thirteen tonnes of propellant every second of its flight.
The Saturn V stood 110 metres tall and weighed about 2,900 tonnes when fuelled.
At liftoff most of the mass is fuel; the Apollo capsule was a tiny fraction of the stack.
Thirteen Saturn Vs flew between 1967 and 1973, and every single one succeeded.
The five F-1 engines produced about thirty-four million newtons of thrust during flight.
NASA's Space Launch System is ninety-eight metres tall and produces more power than the Saturn V.
The Artemis I mission generated thirty-nine million newtons of thrust at liftoff in 2022.
The sound of a Saturn V launch was among the loudest ever produced by a machine.
Both rockets demonstrate immense scale, with the Space Launch System exceeding the Saturn V in liftoff thrust.
